say.en: Your phone suggests the next word as you type, and a map app finds a route around a traffic jam. Nobody wrote a rule for every case. How does the machine know? In this lesson: Define artificial intelligence.
Explain how machine learning uses training and testing data.
Give everyday applications of natural language processing.

body.en: Emerging trends are new technologies that are expected to change how we live and work. *Artificial Intelligence* (AI) aims to make machines mimic human intelligence: learning, reasoning and solving problems. Machine Learning (ML) is a part of AI in which a computer learns from data instead of being explicitly programmed with rules. An ML model is built using training data, and its accuracy is then checked with testing data it has not seen. Once accurate, it predicts results for new data, as in spam filters and product recommendations.

points.en: AI: *machines* that learn, reason and solve problems
ML: *learning* from data, a subset of AI
Training data builds the model; testing data checks it
Examples: spam filters, recommendations, face unlock

title.en: How a machine learns: fit a line

narration.en: Machine learning finds a rule from examples. Here each green dot is a student: hours studied and marks. The model is marks = w × hours + b. Learning means choosing w and b to make the error (the red gaps) as small as possible. Move w and b to make the error as small as you can. Show the best fit. How close did you get? What does it predict for 9 hours?
narration.kn: ಯಂತ್ರ ಕಲಿಕೆ ಉದಾಹರಣೆಗಳಿಂದ ನಿಯಮ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ಹಸಿರು ಚುಕ್ಕೆ ಒಬ್ಬ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿ: ಓದಿದ ಗಂಟೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅಂಕ. ಮಾದರಿ ಅಂಕ = w × ಗಂಟೆ + b. ಕಲಿಕೆ ಎಂದರೆ ದೋಷ (ಕೆಂಪು ಅಂತರ) ಕನಿಷ್ಠವಾಗುವಂತೆ w, b ಆರಿಸುವುದು. ದೋಷ ಆದಷ್ಟು ಕಡಿಮೆ ಆಗುವಂತೆ w ಮತ್ತು b ಸರಿಸಿ. ಅತ್ಯುತ್ತಮ ರೇಖೆ ತೋರಿಸಿ. ನೀವು ಎಷ್ಟು ಹತ್ತಿರ ಬಂದಿರಿ? 9 ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಏನು ಊಹಿಸುತ್ತದೆ?

title.en: On the board: AI, machine learning and NLP

say.en: Artificial intelligence is the big idea: machines that learn, reason and solve problems like people.
Machine learning is a part of AI. The computer learns patterns from data instead of being told every rule.
Natural language processing overlaps with AI: it lets computers understand and produce human speech and text.
Here is how a machine learning model is built. First it is trained on many labelled examples.
Then new, unseen data is given to the model, and it predicts the answer.
The more good examples it sees, the better its predictions become.

narration.en: We place machine learning inside artificial intelligence, add natural language processing, and follow how a model learns from data.

body.en: *Natural Language Processing* (NLP) deals with the interaction between computers and human languages. It lets a computer understand, translate and produce speech and text. Voice assistants, speech-to-text typing, machine translation between languages, spell checkers, predictive typing and chatbots on customer-care websites all use NLP.

heading.en: AI, Machine Learning, NLP, VR/AR and Robotics

tagline.en: What artificial intelligence is, how machine learning learns from training data, everyday natural language processing, virtual versus augmented reality, and robots and drones.

myth.en: AR and VR are the same thing; both just mean wearing a headset to see 3D images.

truth.en: VR replaces your surroundings with a computer-generated world. AR adds digital objects or information to the real world you still see, often through only a phone camera. Both are called immersive experiences and both show 3D graphics, so they are easily mixed up. The test is simple: can you still see the real world?

say.en: AI makes machines imitate human intelligence: learning, reasoning and decision making.
ML is a part of AI: a model learns patterns from training data and is checked on testing data.
NLP: computers understanding human language (auto-correct, translation, chatbots, sentiment analysis).
VR replaces the real world with a simulated one; AR adds digital content to the real world.
Robots perform tasks automatically using sensors and programs; drones are unmanned aircraft.

problem.en: A college wants software that marks an email as "spam" or "not spam". Describe how machine learning would do it.

steps.en: Collect thousands of old emails already labelled spam or not spam.
Use most of them as training data to build a model that learns patterns in spam.
Check the model's accuracy on the remaining emails (testing data).
Use the trained model to label new incoming emails.

answer.en: Train on labelled emails, test on unseen ones, then classify new emails automatically.
